detailed_description: The PDF to Image tool converts selected PDF pages into PNG or JPEG images in your browser. It uses PDF.js to load the PDF, render page previews, and rasterize selected pages to canvas before saving the result. You can choose PNG or JPEG output, select 72, 150, or 300 DPI, and pick the pages you want from the preview grid. A single selected page downloads as an image file, while multiple selected pages are packaged into a ZIP archive. This is useful for creating quick page previews, sharing a page image, or turning PDF pages into image files for workflows that do not accept PDF uploads.
usage_steps: Click the upload area and select a PDF file from your device
Wait for the page previews to load in the browser
Choose PNG or JPEG as the output image format
Select 72, 150, or 300 DPI based on the image size you need
Select or deselect pages from the preview grid
Click Convert to download one image or a ZIP file for multiple pages
usage_examples: A designer exports a page from a PDF report as a PNG preview for a presentation
An online course instructor converts PDF quizzes to JPEG images for embedding in LMS platforms that block PDF uploads
An office worker converts selected PDF pages into images for quick sharing in a chat or document
A developer converts PDF invoices to optimized JPEGs for a legacy CMS that lacks PDF rendering capabilities

faqs.question: How does the PDF to Image converter work?
faqs.answer: It loads your PDF with PDF.js directly in the browser, renders each selected page to a canvas, and saves the rasterized page as a PNG or JPEG file. The PDF never leaves your device.

faqs.question: Which output formats and resolutions are available?
faqs.answer: You can export PNG for lossless quality or JPEG for smaller files, at 72, 150, or 300 DPI. Use 300 DPI when the image will be printed and 72 or 150 DPI for screen use.

faqs.question: Can I convert only specific pages?
faqs.answer: Yes. After the PDF loads, page previews let you pick exactly the pages you want to export, so a 50-page document does not have to be rasterized in full.

faqs.question: Is there a file size or page limit?
faqs.answer: There is no server-side limit because nothing is uploaded. Very large PDFs are constrained only by your browser's available memory, so very long documents are best converted in page batches.

faqs.question: Will scanned or image-based PDFs convert cleanly?
faqs.answer: Image-based pages rasterize faithfully because each page is rendered as it appears. Text-based pages stay crisp at higher DPI settings; scanned pages depend on the quality of the original scan.
